title: Transformer architecture to large foundation-model systems
sourceNativeSummary: The Transformer trajectory is not one algorithm winning one benchmark: a parallelizable architecture became a scaling substrate, then a multimodal model platform, and finally a component inside agentic systems. Each transition introduced new complements and new failure/evaluation boundaries.
rivalOrBoundary: The trajectory is not “one paper caused AI”; architecture, accelerator infrastructure, scaling practice, data, evaluation, deployment and feedback co-evolved.

sourceBundle.title: Attention Is All You Need
sourceBundle.supports: 2017 architecture, baseline comparison and training-parallelism claim

sourceBundle.title: GPT-4 research release
sourceBundle.supports: large multimodal realization, benchmark performance and explicit limitations

pressure: Sequence models based on recurrence or convolution struggled with long-range dependency paths and parallel training efficiency as model/data scale grew.
preExistingWorldModel: Attention mechanisms were useful components inside recurrent sequence models; GPUs/TPUs and large text corpora made high-throughput training increasingly important, but no dominant architecture had eliminated recurrence/convolution for general sequence modeling.
candidateRoutes: replace recurrence/convolution with self-attention and positional information
build task-specific architectures instead of a common pretraining substrate
observationsAndInstruments: The 2017 Transformer paper showed a sequence architecture based entirely on attention, improving machine-translation quality while making training substantially more parallelizable.

The architecture transferred into large-scale pretraining systems and, by 2023, GPT-4 demonstrated a large multimodal model with strong benchmark/professional-task performance while explicitly retaining limitations and safety/evaluation concerns.
By 2025 agentic systems were adding browser/computer/action loops around large models, showing a further realization layer beyond next-token/model capability.
decisiveTests: translation/sequence benchmark quality against strong recurrent/convolutional baselines
transfer across materially different tasks/modalities after pretraining
real-world evaluation, adversarial testing and action reliability when models are embedded in consequence-bearing systems
technicalOrScientificTransition: A training-efficient sequence architecture became a general model substrate through scaling, pretraining and multimodality, then began to acquire separate tool/action/harness layers; architectural representation, model capability and operational agency are distinct historical phases.
rivalsAndFailures: Recurrence/convolution did not become universally useless; local/domain architectures remain competitive under different objectives.
Benchmark and exam performance does not establish reliable real-world action, truthfulness, safety or economic value.
Scaling a model does not automatically create persistent state, authority, verification or operational recovery semantics.
diffusionAndScaling: Transformer-style models diffused from translation into language, vision, multimodal and scientific systems, with model and infrastructure scale increasing by orders of magnitude.
standardsAndInstitutions: Research labs and firms own model releases; benchmark communities, external evaluators, regulators and downstream application owners establish different claims about capability/use.
externalitiesAndCorrections: Compute concentration, data provenance, hallucination, misuse, labor/market effects, energy use and evaluator gaming are separate from benchmark capability.
secondOrderEffects: Large pretrained models lowered the cost of generating and transforming symbolic artifacts and enabled agentic tool-use layers, moving bottlenecks toward evaluation, world grounding, authority, memory/context and reliable action.
unresolvedHistoricalQuestions: Which complement was rate-limiting at each lifecycle phase?
Which later success narrative compresses failures, rivals or distributed contributions?
